summary: Spine documents now include the original Complaint (#1), FAC (#32), SAC (#170), PI motion/ruling (#46, #121), MTD and counterclaim rulings (#163, #228), MSJ briefing/ruling (#327, #329, #350, #390), the four pretrial orders (#446, #452, #456, #477), the remedies/waiver fight (#392, #459-#462, #484-#497), proposed findings (#502-#504), and first-week trial dispute briefs (#508, #511-#516, #522). The list remains curated, not a docket mirror.

entries.notes: Names Aestas Management Co., Aestas LLC, Altman, Brockman, and the OpenAI corporate web. 26 claims. Mooted by the FAC.

entries.label: Order
entries.title: Order on Motions to Dismiss FAC
entries.notes: The single most important pretrial pleading-stage ruling. Express contract dismissed w/o leave; implied contract, fraud and constructive fraud, charitable trust survive; Microsoft survives on tortious interference and aiding-and-abetting fiduciary duty; RICO §1962(c) granted leave; (a)(b) without leave; derivative claims dismissed.

entries.label: Amended Complaint

entries.label: Answer & Counterclaim

entries.label: Order

entries.notes: Strikes 16 of 55 affirmative defenses; pointed criticism of both sides' 'gamesmanship'.

entries.label: Order

entries.notes: Counterclaims survive (UCL + tortious interference w/ prospective economic advantage). RICO and implied covenant on the SAC dismissed without leave. LOI litigation-privilege analysis at p.5–7.

entries.label: Order
entries.title: Order Re Trial Date — Jury Selection 4/27/2026; Jury Trial 4/28/2026
entries.notes: Cements the trial calendar after the MSJ hearing (Jan 7). Drives every downstream pretrial deadline.

entries.label: Order
entries.title: Order on Motion for Summary Judgment
entries.notes: The operative ruling defining what the jury hears. DENIES OpenAI defendants' MSJ in full — Counts IV (unjust enrichment), VI (constructive fraud), VII (fraud), and XVIII (breach of charitable trust) all SURVIVE. GRANTS Microsoft's MSJ as to Counts IV (unjust enrichment) and V (tortious interference); DENIES as to Count XIX (aiding and abetting fiduciary breach), which SURVIVES. Terminates Dkts. 327, 328, 329, 330, 351, 353, 356, 358, 360, 368, 373, 388. This order, not the MTD ruling at #163, is now the spine of the liability case.

entries.label: Notice of Remedies
entries.title: Plaintiffs' Notice of Remedies
entries.notes: First post-MSJ remedies notice. Preserves plaintiffs' position that equitable relief, disgorgement, and claim-specific timing findings would follow liability rather than be fixed by the advisory jury.

entries.label: Daubert Motion
entries.title: Defendants' Motion to Exclude Opinions 3 Through 6 of Dr. C. Paul Wazzan
entries.notes: OpenAI's Daubert challenge to plaintiffs' damages expert. Denied at #452 (PTO #2) but Wazzan was later barred from the liability phase by PTO #4 (#477) — relevance only to remedies.

entries.label: Pretrial Conference Statement
entries.title: Joint Pretrial Conference Statement
entries.notes: Each side's statement of elements and evidence. Frames the disputed legal issues that PTO #3 (#456) then resolved.

entries.title: Proposed Jury Instructions
entries.notes: Both sides' competing instruction sets, plus jury-instruction conference rulings on Day 5 (May 1, 2026).

entries.label: Proposed Form of Verdict
entries.title: Proposed Form of Verdict

entries.label: Pretrial Order No. 1
entries.title: Pretrial Order No. 1
entries.notes: First of four numbered pretrial orders. Sets trial logistics and rulings on the bulk of pretrial motions.

entries.label: Pretrial Order No. 2
entries.title: Pretrial Order No. 2 Re: Motions in Limine and Daubert Motion
entries.notes: Resolves the 12 motions in limine (#402–#415) and OpenAI's Wazzan Daubert motion (#393, denied). Defines what evidence is in/out for trial.

entries.label: Pretrial Order No. 3
entries.title: Pretrial Order No. 3 Re: Disputed Legal Issues (Remedies; Statute of Limitations)
entries.notes: Two structural rulings: (1) disgorgement is an EQUITABLE remedy — judge decides the amount, not jury; (2) statute-of-limitations questions for the jury, but no continuing-violation instruction. The 'remedies = judge' holding is why plaintiffs' demand of up to $134B will be sized by Judge Gonzalez Rogers in the post-jury phase.

entries.label: Amended Notice of Remedies
entries.title: Plaintiffs' Amended Notice of Remedies
entries.notes: Plaintiffs sharpen the remedy ask: return allegedly diverted gains to the OpenAI charity, not to Musk personally; disgorgement and structural relief are framed as charitable-trust remedies.

entries.label: Response
entries.title: Defendants' Response to Amended Notice of Remedies
entries.notes: OpenAI defendants answer that Musk's theories are personal-donation claims, not a vehicle for a public-charity recovery; Microsoft remains implicated only through aiding-and-abetting liability.

entries.label: Reply
entries.title: Plaintiffs' Reply Regarding Amended Notice of Remedies
entries.notes: Plaintiffs defend broad equitable authority to redirect disgorgement and structure relief for the OpenAI charity, including injunctions to enforce charitable obligations.

entries.label: Pretrial Order No. 4
entries.title: Pretrial Order No. 4 Re: Bifurcation and Outstanding Issues Raised in Dkt. No. 468
entries.notes: Bifurcates the trial into LIABILITY phase (Apr 28 – ~May 15) and REMEDIES phase (begins ~May 18). Allots 22 hours each to Musk and OpenAI defendants for liability, 5 hours to Microsoft. Excludes Wazzan from the liability phase (remedies-only relevance). Notes that if the jury finds Musk's action time-barred, the Court will likely accept that finding and direct verdict to defendants.

entries.label: Verified Waiver
entries.title: Musk's Notice Regarding Verified Waiver of Remedies
entries.notes: Musk says he will not seek an award for himself, xAI, or any fund he controls, and prefers any award to go to the OpenAI charity or donor-advised funds directed to donate to it. Defendants attack the waiver as incomplete.

entries.label: Notice
entries.title: Musk's Notice Regarding Fraud Claims
entries.notes: Musk proposes to dismiss fraud and constructive fraud if the court proceeds on charitable trust and unjust enrichment, explicitly to streamline trial around charitable mission and equitable relief.

entries.label: Response
entries.title: OpenAI Defendants' Response to Waiver and Fraud Notices
entries.notes: Defendants argue the waiver undercuts personal-injury standing and ask the court to require an unconditional fraud dismissal and a fuller waiver of all remedies in which Musk has any interest.

entries.label: Joinder
entries.title: Microsoft's Response to Waiver Notices and Joinder
entries.notes: Microsoft joins OpenAI's response and preserves Microsoft-specific arguments about restitution, unclean hands, and the effect of Musk disclaiming a personal recovery.

entries.label: Order
entries.title: Order Denying Emergency Motion to Intervene
entries.notes: Denies #457 motion to intervene filed by a third party shortly before trial.

entries.label: Order
entries.title: Order Deeming Fraud and Constructive Fraud Claims Dismissed With Prejudice
entries.notes: Posture-changing order: Counts VI and VII are voluntarily dismissed with prejudice. The April liability phase is reduced to charitable trust, unjust enrichment/restitution, and Microsoft aiding-and-abetting.

entries.label: Proposed Findings
entries.title: OpenAI Defendants' Proposed Findings of Fact
entries.notes: OpenAI's bench-trial/advisory-jury roadmap: indirect unrestricted donations, no donor restrictions, no breach, and limitations. It is the defense's cleanest late-stage statement of the liability theory.

entries.label: Proposed Findings
entries.title: Musk's Proposed Findings of Fact
entries.notes: Plaintiffs' trial roadmap: founding assurances created a charitable mission, the conversion diverted charitable assets, Microsoft knew enough to aid the breach, and restitution follows.

entries.label: Proposed Findings
entries.title: Microsoft's Proposed Findings of Fact as to Liability
entries.notes: Microsoft's separate roadmap: 'not Microsoft's dispute,' no knowledge of Musk-specific trust duties, no substantial assistance, and defenses of limitations, laches, and unclean hands.

entries.label: Notice
entries.title: OpenAI Defendants' Notice Regarding Curative Instruction
entries.notes: Defendants seek a curative instruction after Musk testified that an adverse ruling would destroy charitable giving in America. Useful for the trial-rhetoric record, not a merits ruling.

entries.label: Minute Entry
entries.title: Jury Trial — Begun
entries.notes: Court reporter Irene Rodriguez. Day 2 first substantive testimony day after Apr 27 jury selection.

entries.label: Notice
entries.title: OpenAI Defendants' Memorandum Regarding Dr. Russell's Testimony
entries.notes: Defendants seek to bar undisclosed AI-risk opinions, including climate-risk and concentration-risk theories, from Stuart Russell's testimony.

entries.label: Joinder
entries.title: Microsoft Joinder Regarding Dr. Russell's Testimony
entries.notes: Microsoft joins OpenAI's Russell-testimony objection.

entries.label: Trial Brief
entries.title: Musk Brief on Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §17510.8
entries.notes: Musk argues §17510.8 independently creates a fiduciary relationship and charitable trust from Altman's 2016 asks and OpenAI's July 2020 rent solicitation; he says §17510.6's membership exclusion does not apply.

entries.label: Trial Brief
entries.title: OpenAI Defendants' Brief Regarding Charitable Solicitations Statute
entries.notes: OpenAI argues §17510.6 excludes member solicitations, Cohen controls, and the July 2020 rent email was at most a $580k rent-specific request already used for rent.

entries.label: Trial Brief
entries.title: OpenAI Defendants' Application to Introduce Evidence of Pretrial Communication
entries.notes: Latest substantive filing in the archive: OpenAI seeks to elicit Brockman testimony that Musk threatened Altman and Brockman would become the most hated men in America, offered for motive and bias rather than liability.
